contains_no_content_of_requested_type.description: True only if the input presents no specific dish together with any of its ingredients or method: equipment, butchery or technique videos without a finished dish, vlogs, product or software videos, and compilations that only name dishes. A video that names a dish and gives its ingredients (even without method) or its method (even without quantities) is NOT empty. Otherwise false.

entries.description: Recipes presented in this video; empty array if none. The input bundles one video: metadata, description, optionally a structured recipe from a page the creator linked, and a transcript. SEGMENTATION: one entry per dish that can be served on its own. A sauce, dressing, spice mix, or garnish made for a dish stays inside that dish's entry; it is its own entry only when the video teaches it as a standalone recipe (a video on five sauces yields five entries). Multi-dish videos ('5 dinners', 'three one-pot meals') yield one entry per dish. A meal-prep bowl built from components is one entry. Create an entry whenever a specific dish comes with its ingredients or its method, even partially (an ingredient list in the description with no written method, or narration of the steps without quantities): fill the missing part from standard practice for that dish, mark reconstructed quantities '(approx.)', and add a cooking_tips line stating what was reconstructed. Dishes only named or shown, with neither ingredients nor method in the input, are not entries. SOURCE PRIORITY: ingredient names and quantities come first from the linked recipe, then the description, then the transcript; technique detail (heat, timing, doneness cues, order of steps) comes from the transcript where it adds to the written sources. Transcripts are often unpunctuated automatic speech recognition: correct obvious misrecognitions of ingredient and dish names silently.

title_original.description: Dish title as the video presents it, in its original language (from the video title, description, or narration). Null if the dish is never named.

title_modern_english.description: English rendering of title_original without hashtags, emojis, or clickbait phrasing ('The BEST Gazpacho' -> 'Gazpacho'). Null only if title_original is null and no name can be inferred.

dish_name_generic.description: The conventional English dish name a cookbook index would use, lowercase, without creator, brand, or diet qualifiers: 'tarte tatin', 'chicken biryani', 'pasta e fagioli', 'white bean stew'. Used to find historical counterparts, so prefer the established name of the dish family over a descriptive invention.

recipe_type.description: Primary category of the dish. Ferments of vegetables are 'Preserve'; fermented drinks (tepache, kombucha, mead) are 'Brewing'; stocks, doughs, and demi-glace are 'Preparation Technique'.

cuisine.description: Cuisine or regional tradition in English ('Lebanese', 'Northern Italian', 'Sichuan', 'Korean-Mexican fusion'), as stated or clearly implied by the dish. Null for dishes without a recognizable tradition.

recipe_text_modern_english.description: A complete recipe in English that someone could cook from: first 'Ingredients:' as one line per ingredient with quantity, then 'Method:' as numbered steps with heat levels, times, and doneness cues. Where no source gives a quantity, write 'to taste' or give the amount shown or implied and mark it '(approx.)'. No creator banter, sponsorships, or calls to subscribe.

ingredients.description: Every ingredient of this dish, including those of its internal sauces and garnishes.

name_original.description: Ingredient name as written or spoken in the source, original language.

name_modern_english.description: Generic English ingredient name, lowercase singular, without brand or preparation ('chickpea', 'gochujang', 'parmesan', 'plant-based butter'). Used for ingredient-on-hand search.

quantity_original.description: Quantity as given in the source ('200 g', '1 tbsp', 'a handful'). Null if unstated.

is_main_ingredient.description: True for the ingredients that define the dish or make up most of its volume (typically two to five per dish). False for seasonings, oils, garnishes, and minor aromatics.

cooking_methods.description: Cooking techniques used (braising, stir-frying, pressure cooking, fermenting). Empty if none.

method_modern_english.description: Technique in plain English, lowercase gerund ('braising').

utensils_equipment.description: Equipment beyond a standard stove, oven, pot, pan, knife, and board: e.g. pressure cooker, blender, stand mixer, air fryer, cast-iron skillet, tart tin, thermometer. Empty if none.

timing_yield.description: Yield and times as stated in the sources; null for unstated fields.

yield_original.description: Yield as stated ('serves 4', '12 cookies', '5 meal-prep portions').

total_time_minutes.description: Estimated minutes from start to serving, active plus passive, excluding any single wait longer than 2 hours (soaking, marinating, proofing, fermenting), which is flagged in requires_advance_prep. Use stated times where given, otherwise estimate from the steps. Null only if no estimate is possible.

requires_advance_prep.description: True if the recipe needs a wait longer than 2 hours or prior-day preparation (overnight soaking, marinating, proofing, fermenting).

difficulty_1_3.description: 1 = easy (basic techniques, forgiving); 2 = moderate (several components or timing-sensitive steps); 3 = demanding (advanced technique such as laminated or spun-sugar work, precise temperatures, or long multi-stage preparation).

ingredient_categories.description: Boolean ingredient flags. Plant-based substitutes (vegan butter, oat milk, vegan cheese, egg replacer, plant-based mince) never set the animal-product flags.

contains_meat.description: Red meat from mammals (beef, pork, lamb, veal, game), including stocks and cured meats. Excludes poultry and fish.

contains_poultry.description: Chicken, duck, turkey, or other birds, including chicken stock.

contains_fish_seafood.description: Fish, shellfish, or seafood, including fish sauce, anchovy, and dashi from bonito.

contains_dairy.description: Milk, cream, cheese, yogurt, or other dairy. Butter has its own flag.

contains_lard_animal_fat.description: Lard, tallow, duck fat, bacon fat, or other animal fat that is not butter.

contains_alcohol.description: Wine, beer, spirits, mirin, or other alcoholic ingredient.

contains_other_sweeteners.description: Maple syrup, agave, molasses, date syrup, or dried fruit used as sweetener.

contains_foreign_spices.description: Spices of long-distance trade origin (pepper, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, ginger, saffron, cardamom, cumin, chili). Excludes local herbs.

contains_luxury_ingredients.description: Costly ingredients such as truffle, caviar, saffron in quantity, wagyu, lobster, or premium aged cheese.

contains_gluten.description: Wheat, barley, rye, spelt, or products made from them (flour, bread, pasta, soy sauce unless tamari, seitan).

protein_rich.description: True if the dish supplies roughly 20 g protein or more per serving, or the video presents it as high-protein.

occasion.description: Occasions the dish suits, as presented or clearly implied. Empty if unclear.

season.description: Seasons the dish suits, by its produce or framing ('cozy winter stew', 'summer salad'). ['All year'] if not seasonal.

sources_used.description: Which parts of the input this entry draws on.

cooking_tips.description: Practical tips given in the video beyond the steps (substitutions, make-ahead, storage, common mistakes), one short English sentence each. Empty if none.
